title: A near-balanced subprotocol
statement:
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol, and let $n$ be a natural number with $n > 1$. Write $\ell(q)$ for the number of leaves of a protocol $q$, and suppose that $3\,\ell(p) \ge 2n$. Then there is a subprotocol $s$ of $p$ (a rooted subtree of $p$) whose leaf count satisfies
\[
n \le 3\,\ell(s) < 2n.
\]
hypotheses_covered: s is a subprotocol of p
replaced:
Given a protocol $p$ with $3 \cdot p.\mathrm{numLeaves} \ge 2n$ and $n > 1$, there exists a
subprotocol $s$ of $p$ satisfying $n \le 3 \cdot s.\mathrm{numLeaves} < 2n$.  This is the
inductive step used to prove the balanced subprotocol theorem.
